Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:129: And a person acquires all this attribute of humility now through acquiring holiness - for whoever walks after the stubbornness of his heart in the desires of this world thinks that the whole world is his, and none acquires the attribute of humility except one who is stripped of the affairs of matter and physicality, as explained; for the arrogant one, the world does not suffice for the height of his heart. But the discerning one, when he contemplates that all the goods of this world are a passing shadow and a withering flower, that a person himself is here today and tomorrow in the grave, and that there is no reality of a dwelling for the soul in this world at all, but everything is to prepare him for his eternal home - he separates from the desires of this world and draws upon himself holiness, in order to cleave to his Creator, who is the true purpose, for whose reward the soul waits, to shine in the light of life.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:130: Like the parable of a person whose eyes are open, who sees the sweetness of light, and at some time it happens that he becomes blind - that person waits forever for when the veil of blindness will be removed from his eyes through good ointments, so that he may return to seeing the bright light. So the soul, hewn from the light of the supernal life in the supernal world, when the Holy One, blessed be He, imprisons it in this turbid body, the sight of the supernal lights becomes sealed from it - and the discerning person takes for himself the ointment of the holiness of Torah and commandments, and through this his soul is sanctified and cleaves to the bright light, which is the light of Torah, called "light," as it is written (Proverbs 6:23), "and Torah is light" - and he repents, to remove the partition separating between him and his God. And even though he will suffer - for even the blind man suffers when his eyes are treated, whether with a strong salve or something else, and nevertheless he endures it in order to see the light, and sometimes he suffers over the doubt whether it will help or not - but one who suffers through repentance certainly benefits by removing the blindness of his soul, through which it cleaves to the Creator, and through this the veil of matter is removed from it; for even though it remains clothed in matter, the light of the soul will increase over the body, and the body will not be a veil separating between it and its God - and this is the acquisition of the attributes stated in this discourse, up to the attribute of holiness, which is to remove the veil separating from the soul until it cleaves to the Creator. And the other attributes mentioned - humility, fear, and piety - are all links of one chain that unfold from holiness, for holiness is their father, and humility and the rest are its offspring; for just as one has holiness, humility must necessarily follow, as explained. And with all this, one must give a connection and relation between humility and fear of sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:131: And when the reader considers what was explained in the Gate of Holiness concerning the holiness of each and every limb, he will see that humility must necessarily follow holiness, and they are one bond, brothers who will not be separated - for if he sanctifies his eyes as stated there, he thereby has lowered eyes, which is one of the conditions of humility. And if he sanctifies his tongue as stated there, certainly he will not utter insults from his mouth as one who is angry does. And if he sanctifies his heart, he must distance from it envy and hatred - behold, he is humble. It follows that all the conditions of humility and its particulars depend on a person's sanctifying himself properly, as we explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:132: Further, it is possible to give another connection and relation of holiness to humility, and through it may be understood the reason and connection of humility to fear of sin. And the matter is that the essence of holiness depends on the holiness of thought, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayetze, page 155a), whose words we copied in the Gate of Holiness - that concerning the holiness of thought it is said (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and it is impossible for the holiness of thought to come except through the soul, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:133: And in the Zohar (Parashat Tetzaveh, page 182a), in the explanation of the verse (Isaiah 2:22), "cease from man, whose breath [neshamah] is in his nostrils" - he said there that when a person is angry, the soul departs from him - and not specifically the neshamah, but even the nefesh, as it is written (Job 18:4), "he tears his soul [nafsho] in his anger." And through this may be understood the precision of his wording there, where he says, "and he has the holy spirit [ru'ach] within him, which comprises three," as we have established that there is nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah. And he further says on: for these three powers are all one. And this whole introduction is to reconcile the verses, since one verse says "he tears his soul [nefesh] in his anger," and one verse says "whose breath [neshamah] is in his nostrils" - and for this he preceded and said that all three are one bond, and all of them depart, and the blemish is in all of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:134: And so he further says on: and not only that, but the supernal holiness is uprooted from its place, and a strange god settles in its place. It appears that the whole reality of holiness, from nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, all departs, and a strange god rests there. And he further says: whoever converses with him is as one who has literally joined himself to idolatry - and if some ru'ach or nefesh had remained, it would not be literal idolatry, for there would still be some holiness in him; rather, certainly all of it departs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:135: And we are compelled to say that this blemish that reaches the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah are not the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah of Atzilut, but the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah [or: from the mode of the Chariot and the Throne] - which the blemish blemishes, for the intent is not merely departure, but that they are actually blemished, as they said, of blessed memory: and if he brings that holy soul into another service, this defiles it, and it departs from the service of its Master. And he further says on, that this holy soul is torn and defiled because of his anger, and so on. But concerning the soul of Atzilut, we cannot speak of impurity and blemish, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 98b), in these words: there is an Adam who is an angel, and this is Metatron; and there is an Adam in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is His Atzilut, and this is yud-heh-vav-heh, alef-dalet-nun-yud - and he has no Beriah, Yetzirah, or Asiyah, only Atzilut, and in this place there is no sin and no death - this is what is written (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:136: And if a blemish is found in one who has a soul of Atzilut, it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 124a) that the intent is not an actual blemish, that would darken its light, but rather the departure of the soul of Atzilut is the "blemish" that reaches it - and we copied this discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:137: And behold, based on these introductions from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, we can say that what the discourse says, "holiness brings one to humility," is this: whoever merits the soul of Atzilut, who is certainly holy, as we copied the discourse of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4, will merit humility, so that he not come to anger in a way that would blemish the soul - for that supernal holy soul will not be given to one who blemishes it, at every time it departs from him; for the angry person, having that evil attribute, becomes angry over a trivial thing. Rather, certainly, once he has already merited the soul of Atzilut, which is holy, it will bring him to humility, so that his inclination is subdued in such a way that holiness not be lost from him, and it shall be fulfilled in him (Proverbs 12:28), "no harm shall befall the righteous." And one who has not merited the holy soul, in whom the external force still has some grip, will also be brought to anger, so that a strange god rest in him, because he has not been purified from his iniquities as is fitting. Therefore he must strive to attain the attribute of humility through all the aforementioned attributes, until he attains holiness - and since he is holy and the external impurity has no part in him, certainly it will not defile him through anger, which defiles him from within and from without, as explained there in Parashat Tetzaveh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:138: And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, because of the merit of his supernal soul, had great humility - "and the man Moses was very humble, more than any man," and so on (Numbers 12:3) - and yet, nevertheless, it is said of him (Numbers 31:14), "and Moses was angry," and so on, and they explained, of blessed memory (Vayikra Rabbah 13:1), that a halachah was hidden from him - for according to the subtlety and merit of the soul, a small thing will blemish it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:139: And along these lines we shall understand his saying, "humility brings one to fear of sin" - for "fear of sin" means that he fears lest even a small sin come into his hand, for according to how much he has merited a supernal soul, so must he fear sin. And the parable for this is the stain of oil that falls on garments - for a stain falling on a linen garment is not equal to a stain falling on a fine woolen garment, nor to one falling on garments of silk and embroidery. So the reality of the blemish is not equal for one who has a nefesh, one who has a ru'ach, and one who has a neshamah - and this is what they explained, of blessed memory (Yevamot 121b), on "and all around Him it storms mightily" (Psalms 50:3) - the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous to a hairsbreadth, for a hairsbreadth is a great blemish according to the subtlety of their soul, like a great iniquity is to the rest of the people, [as heavy as] the rope of a wagon.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:140: And it is possible that this is why Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai trembled at the hour of his death (Berachot 28b), saying, "I do not know by which path they are leading me" - for according to his wisdom, he certainly merited a supernal soul, and a small blemish would be considered great.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:141: And whoever merits humility will merit fear of sin, and it follows of itself - for just as he guards himself from anger so that his soul not depart from him, and cause "one sinner to destroy much good" (Ecclesiastes 9:18) - for they said in Parashat Tetzaveh that after a person sins through anger, would that he be resanctified, because a strange god rests in his body and does not depart easily - therefore he shall fear sin, from blemishing again, even a small sin, so as not to lose the virtue of his soul; for sometimes the blemish will be such that the holy spiritual soul departs and does not return again, and it is a loss that does not come back, and it will require many preparations until it returns to how it was - would that it return.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:142: And according to the ways I explained above concerning "holiness brings one to humility," by these same ways the matter of fear of sin will also be settled - for the one who sins literally before the king is not comparable to one who is in his courtyard, or one who is in his province; so too, one who draws near to the Holy One, blessed be He, through his good deeds, and thinks that he stands before Him always, and because of this has humility, as explained - for this same reason he will fear sin, even a small sin, for he will be ashamed to sin before the King before whom he stands, for it is not fitting to provoke the King in any small or great matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:143: "Fear of sin brings one to..." and so on. All that we intended to explain in this beraita is to explain the attribute of piety [chassidut], for it is the acquisition of the attribute of love, as it is written (Psalms 31:24), "love the LORD, all His pious ones" - for whoever reaches the level called "chassid" is a lover, and the holy spirit rests upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:144: And behold, the attribute of piety, in general, is to conduct himself in all his affairs beyond the letter of the law, as they say in the Gemara (cf. Yerushalmi, chapter 8, halachah 4): "is this not the teaching of the pious - one must act beyond the letter of the law"? And this attribute is one of His attributes, blessed be He, through which He conducts Himself with His creatures, as it is written (Micah 7:18), "for He delights in kindness [chesed]," and likewise (Exodus 34:7), "keeping kindness for thousands," and "abundant in kindness" (ibid. 34:6), and many similar verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:145: And after a person is complete in fear, so that he does not sin even a small sin, he transcends the attribute of judgment and the attribute of kindness rests upon him. And the reason is that when a person sins even a little, the attribute of judgment necessarily must be with him to purify and chastise him for that blemish, and when the judgment against him is complete, then kindness receives him - and this is the reason Michael brings near the souls of the righteous (Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha, page 80a; Tosafot Menachot 110a), for the right is what brings near after the souls have been purified from the River of Fire (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, page 211a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:146: And behold, the attribute of Chesed has branches, and whoever wishes to merit it must hold fast to its branches, and the branches of Chesed are explained in Scripture. The first attribute one must hold from Chesed is the Torah, which flows from it, as it is said (Proverbs 31:26), "and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue," and as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 5), "nor is an ignorant person [am ha'aretz] pious" - and he explained, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, page 33a), a sweet matter concerning this: he said that the Torah flows from Chochmah, which is the yud, and the chassid is called "chesed" when he brings the yud, which is Chochmah, into it - namely, "chesed-yud" - and the ignorant person, who has not merited Torah, has not merited Chochmah, and therefore it is not fitting for him to be called "chassid," for he lacks the yud.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:147: And further, in order to merit this, one must occupy himself with Torah from midnight onward until the light of morning, in order to receive the thread of kindness that flows from Chesed upon the Shechinah, and upon those occupied in Torah who have taken hold of her - as they elaborated in the Zohar in several places, and especially in Parashat Vayikra (21b) - and this is what they said, of blessed memory (Chagigah 12b): whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, a thread of kindness is drawn upon him by day - and "night" is called [in this context] after midnight, for before midnight it is called "eve," as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 20).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:148: Further, among the attributes of Chesed is to hold fast to charity and acts of kindness in all their particulars, as will be explained in its place, with God's help - for all these are branches of Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:149: Further, one must fast if he has the strength, as they said in Ta'anit (11a-b): if he can afflict himself, he is called holy; and if not, he is called a sinner. And if he can afflict himself, he is called holy and pious, for it is written (Proverbs 11:17), "a man of kindness rewards his own soul." And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit, ibid.), in these words: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, whoever sits in a fast is called pious, as it is said, "a man of kindness rewards his own soul." And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "rewards his own soul" as one who separates his soul from food and drink, as in "on the day Isaac was weaned" [gomel]," from my teacher's mouth. Alternatively, "gomel" is a term for reward, meaning he completes his soul for his Owner.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:150: And the reason he is called "a man of kindness" may be said based on what they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 20b), that it is like the image of the rose, which is red and white, and when it is pressed by fire, everything turns white, for the water that comes out is white. So too one who sits in a fast and diminishes his fat and blood, and the fire prevails over him - the fragrance rising from his mouth is like the fragrance of the sacrifice that was reduced through fire and turned white, and he is atoned for. It follows from this that he is called by [the attribute of] Chesed, which is whiteness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:151: And certainly the words of Reish Lakish are said only of one who has sinned and needs to repent - for if he fasts, he is called "a man of kindness." And the reason is that since he sinned through the sustenance that flowed to him from the side of Chesed, he must reward his soul from sustenance, eating and drinking, and thereby he pays it reward measure for measure - "with what it sinned, it shall be punished," for a person sins only through eating and drinking, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. But a Torah scholar who has not sinned need not fast - and the proof is from Hillel the Elder, as we shall copy shortly - for because he was pious, in that he never in his life grew angry, he would eat as an act of kindness to his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:152: And further, Reish Lakish himself said there that a Torah scholar is not permitted to fast, in these words: Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said in the name of Reish Lakish, a Torah scholar is not permitted to sit in a fast, because it diminishes the work of Heaven - to this point. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "it diminishes the work of Heaven" - he becomes weak and cannot study.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:153: And in our time, no Torah scholar is free of sin, especially from slander or the other categories that do not receive the presence of the Shechinah, and therefore it is fitting that he fast. And should you say that Torah atones for sin, I answer you from King David, peace be upon him, who was a Torah scholar, head of the Sanhedrin, and nevertheless all his days were in fasting after he sinned, as we shall explain in the Gate of Repentance (chapter 3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:154: And further, it is possible to give another reason why one who fasts is fittingly called "chassid": because one who eats is sustained according to the nature of the world, like the other creatures that eat to sustain their bodies, and the world was created according to nature, which is "Elohim" - for "ha-teva" [nature] equals in numerical value "Elohim" - and therefore the world was created with Elohim, "in the beginning God [Elohim] created" (Genesis 1:1), and the name "Elohim" is mentioned there thirty-two times, and all things that follow nature - such as oil that ignites and water that extinguishes fire - this is according to nature. And behold, the pious one reverses nature and says, "He who said to the oil that it should burn, can say to vinegar that it should burn" (Ta'anit 25a). And along these lines, one who fasts, not wishing to conduct himself according to nature like the other creatures, certainly his sustenance is according to Chesed, which is a subtle, spiritual sustenance - and this is along the lines of the sustenance of Torah scholars, whose sustenance is the sustenance of the soul, flowing from Chochmah, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. And therefore it is fitting that he be called "chassid" - "chesed-yud" - for the yud partners with Chesed to sustain the pious who hold fast to the Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:155: And so you will find that the angels are sustained from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 104a). And therefore souls in the World to Come are sustained from the side of Chesed, for the soul is called "the daughter of a priest," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, pages 95a-b), for it is written (Leviticus 22:12), "and if a priest's daughter marry a stranger, she may not eat of the offering of the holy things" - implying that if she did not marry a stranger, who is the evil inclination, she eats of the offering of the holy things flowing from Chesed, for all holiness is from the side of the right, the yud; and so "she shall eat of her father's bread" indicates this - and so in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 166b), concerning "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance" - see there. And a sign for this matter (Psalms 62:13), "and to You, O LORD, belongs kindness, for You render to a man," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:156: And in any case, if he needs to eat, or to bathe himself in a bathhouse for the health of his body, he is also called "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" - like the deed of Hillel the Elder, peace be upon him, brought in Vayikra Rabbah (34:3) on the verse "and if your brother becomes poor" (Leviticus 25:39), in these words: "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" (Proverbs 11:17) - this is Hillel the Elder, who, when he took leave of his students, would walk along with them. They said to him, where are you going? He said to them, to perform a commandment. They said to him, what commandment does Hillel perform? He said to them, to bathe in the bathhouse. They said to him, is this a commandment? He said to them, yes - for if the statues of kings, which are set up in circuses and theaters, the one appointed over them scrubs and washes them, and they raise for him wages - and not only that, but he is elevated among the ranks of the kingdom - how much more so we, who were created in [God's] image and likeness, as it is written (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man." And so Hillel the Elder would say to his students, at the hour he took leave of them: I am going to perform an act of kindness with this guest [ushpiza] who is in my house. They said to him, do you have a guest every day? He said to them, this wretched soul - is it not a guest within the body? For today it is here, and tomorrow it is not here. Another interpretation: "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" - one who distributes charities. "And he who troubles his own flesh is cruel" - Rabbi Alexandri said, this is one to whom joy comes and he does not draw his relatives to him because of their poverty - therefore Moses warns Israel, "you shall surely give to him" - to this point. And "one who distributes charities" - he gives charity, and this is proven in Vayikra Rabbah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:157: Further, one who holds fast to the attribute of Chesed is one who hears his own disgrace and is silent, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 669), on the verse (Psalms 16:10), "You will not give Your pious one to see corruption" - in these words: the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "chassid," as it is said (Jeremiah 3:12), "for I am pious [chassid], says the LORD" - and David called himself "chassid," as it is said (Psalms 86:2), "preserve my soul, for I am pious"; "You will not give Your pious one to see corruption" - Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Alexandri: whoever hears his own curse and is silent is called "chassid" - and David heard his curse and was silent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:158: And this attribute is one of the attributes of the lover, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Shabbat 88b) on the verse (Judges 5:31), "and those who love Him shall be like the sun going forth in its strength" - our Rabbis taught: those who are insulted but do not insult, who hear their disgrace and do not respond, who act out of love and rejoice in suffering - of them Scripture says, "and those who love Him shall be like the sun going forth in its strength" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:159: And so among the attributes of Chesed is that he not bear a grudge nor take vengeance nor grow angry - for so the prophet Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 3:12), "return, backsliding Israel, says the LORD; I will not cause My anger to fall upon you, for I am pious, says the LORD; I will not bear a grudge forever."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:160: And the general rule is that since a person transcends the attributes of judgment and cruelty and deals with his fellow creatures beyond the letter of the law, he merits the attribute of Chesed - for by strict law, if he rests without ill will, it would be fitting for him to respond to his disgrace and to be angry with one who has blemished his honor; but one who forgives merits Chesed, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, deals with His creatures in the attribute of Chesed, as it is said (Psalms 103:10), "He has not dealt with us according to our sins."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:161: And concerning this it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145a): we have learned, any person who has piety in him is called "an angel of the LORD of Hosts" - this is what is written (Malachi 2:7), "for the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and Torah they should seek from his mouth, for he is an angel of the LORD of Hosts." And he says, just as Michael is a priest above, from the side of Chesed, so the priest, from the side of Chesed, is an angel of the LORD below; and a person who has piety in him enters beyond the letter of the law with every person - it follows that he does not conduct himself according to the nature of this world, which was created according to the letter of the law, but according to the World to Come, which was created with the yud (Menachot 29b), which is the right, Chochmah, the root of Chesed (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 227b) - and therefore piety is greater than all of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:162: And on the verse "preserve my soul, for I am pious" (Psalms 86:2), this matter is brought (in the Yalkut, ibid., remez 834), and in another version: whoever hears his own disgrace, and it is within his power to protest, but is silent, is called "chassid" - and this version appears more correct.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:163: And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 4a): Rabbi Levi and Rabbi Yitzchak - one said, David said this before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, am I not pious, that all the kings of east and west sleep until the third hour of the day, while I rise at midnight to give thanks to You? And the other said, David said this before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, am I not pious, that all the kings of east and west sit in groups in their honor before them, while my hands are soiled with the blood of a fetus and the afterbirth, in order to purify a woman for her husband; and not only that, but everything I do, I take counsel with Mefivoshet my teacher, and say to him, Mefivoshet my teacher, have I judged rightly, have I found guilty rightly, have I acquitted rightly, have I declared impure rightly, have I declared pure rightly - and I was not ashamed. Rabbi Yehoshua the son of Rav Idi said, what verse [supports this]? (Psalms 119:46), "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:164: We learn from this discourse that one who rises at midnight is called "chassid." And likewise, one who makes himself small before one greater than himself, and is not ashamed to ask him a matter of Torah law, is called "chassid." And the verse Rabbi Yehoshua brought, "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings," we are compelled to say refers, by "kings," to the Sages, as they say (Gittin 62a), "who are 'kings'? These are the Rabbis." And in general we learn from this discourse that anyone who does a thing not obligatory upon him by the law of the Torah is called "chassid" for these matters mentioned in the discourse - to purify a woman for her husband, and the rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:165: Further, among the branches of Chesed is that he rebuke his fellow - and this is an act of kindness, for he does kindness with that soul; and one who is rebuked should accept his fellow's rebuke for the sake of Heaven, and consider that rebuke a kindness done to him, since through it he is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 141:5), "let the righteous strike me, it shall be a kindness; and let him rebuke me." And concerning the matter of rebuke, we elaborated in the Gate of Humility, chapter 5.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:166: Further, among the branches of Chesed is trust in the LORD, as it is said (ibid. 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him." And they said in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Tanchum - even a wicked person, if he trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him - to this point. And the intent is that they expounded the juxtaposition of the verse, "many are the sorrows of the wicked; but he who trusts."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:167: And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Kamma 30a): whoever wishes to be pious should fulfill the matters of Berachot [blessings], and the matters of Nezikin [damages], and the matters of Avot [ethics] - to this point. And the reason for the matters of Berachot is that because he is of a good eye, he shall be blessed, as explained above. And likewise the matters of Nezikin, because one who damages his fellow becomes a portion of the judgment of Gevurah to strike his fellow, and he distances himself from Chesed, which benefits all - therefore he must learn Nezikin so as not to come to damage his fellow. And the matters of Avot are self-evident.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:168: Further, in order to merit Chesed, one must be a God-fearing person, as it is said (Psalms 103:17), "but the kindness of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him" - for the ascent of the levels from below upward is: first one enters through fear, and afterward through Chesed - for the Shechinah is called "fear" (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 229b), and one must hold fast to the particulars of fear that are in her, and afterward ascend to the world of the male, which is Chesed - for the Righteous One [Yesod] is called "Chesed," as explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 142a). And likewise, Chesed [and] Gevurah - Gevurah is called "fear," and one must be careful of the negative commandments, and afterward he shall merit Chesed, which is the fulfillment of the positive commandments; and the particulars of fear are the attributes mentioned - alacrity, cleanliness, purity - and further particulars will be explained in the Gate of Holiness. And all the attributes we have explained in this Gate are the levels that lead to being a chassid.
